newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan minister's son remanded over killing.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan minister's son remanded over killing.

text.p: A Sri Lankan court on Wednesday remanded for a week the son of deputy defence minister Anuruddha Ratwatte over the killing of a Papua New Guinean rugby coach outside a casino in the capital Colombo, court officials said.
Lohan Ratwatte was remanded in custody until June 4 after he was identified by three prosecution witnesses at an identification parade as having been present when PNG coach Joel Pera died, they said.
Pera was shot dead outside the casino on May 1 after an argument.
The court also remanded four others in custody in connection with the killing of Pera, who was the coach at a local rubgy club.

All five are considered suspects in the case and were remanded in custody because the court has no power to grant bail without the advice of the attorney-general in a murder case under Sri Lankan law. None of them has been charged.

Anuruddha Ratwatte, who is also minister for power and irrigation, told parliament on Tuesday that the police inquiry into Pera's killing would be independent and impartial and that he will not interfere with it.
